event.moving.name: Moving
event.moving.title: Moving checklist
event.moving.subtitle: Who to tell when you change address
event.moving.lead: Tell each department. They don’t share your new address.
event.moving.sub: Government systems aren’t connected, so every program that has your address needs the new one.
event.moving.blurb: CRA, Service Canada, IRCC, Elections Canada, passport
event.moving.handoffNote: Find the change-of-address steps for every federal organization.
event.baby.name: Having a baby
event.baby.title: New baby checklist
event.baby.subtitle: Birth registration, benefits and leave
event.baby.lead: Register the birth first: it can start the rest.
event.baby.sub: Some provinces offer a newborn service that also applies for benefits. In every province, you can request your baby’s SIN when you register the birth.
event.baby.blurb: Birth registration, child benefit, parental leave
event.baby.handoffNote: Answer 3 questions for a personalized list on canada.ca.
event.marriage.name: Marriage or name change
event.marriage.title: Marriage and name change checklist
event.marriage.subtitle: Marital status, new name and benefits
event.marriage.lead: Your marital status and your name are separate updates.
event.marriage.sub: Tell the CRA about your new status by the end of the month after it changes. A new name is a few more stops.
event.marriage.date: Date of the marriage or change
event.marriage.handoffNote: Update your marital status, name and contact details with the CRA.
event.job-loss.name: Losing a job
event.job-loss.title: Job loss checklist
event.job-loss.subtitle: Employment Insurance and next steps
event.job-loss.lead: Apply for EI right away, even without your paperwork.
event.job-loss.sub: If you apply more than 4 weeks after your last day of work, you may lose benefits.
event.job-loss.handoffNote: See if you qualify, then apply online. No account needed.
event.retiring.name: Retiring
event.retiring.title: Retirement checklist
event.retiring.subtitle: Public pensions and savings
event.retiring.lead: Your CPP doesn’t start on its own, so plan the dates.
event.retiring.sub: Old Age Security often starts on its own. The Canada Pension Plan never does.
event.retiring.date: When you want your CPP to start
event.retiring.handoffNote: Answer a few questions to get your retirement list.
event.death.name: Death of a loved one
event.death.title: When someone dies
event.death.subtitle: Who to notify and what you may be entitled to
event.death.lead: One step at a time. Not everything has to happen today.
event.death.sub: Here’s what federal departments need to know, and the benefits family members may be able to get.
event.death.blurb: CRA, CPP, survivor benefits, final return
event.death.handoffNote: Answer a few questions to get a checklist for your situation.

task.moving.cra.title: Update your address with the CRA
task.moving.cra.detail: It’s immediate online in your CRA account, under Profile. It keeps benefit payments and tax mail coming to you.
task.moving.sc.title: Update your address with Service Canada
task.moving.sc.detail: Old Age Security and dental care: change it in My Service Canada Account. EI, CPP and the Canada Disability Benefit: call, request a call back or visit a Service Canada Centre.
task.moving.elections.title: Update your voter registration
task.moving.elections.detail: It takes a few minutes online, so your voter information card reaches your new home when an election is called.
task.moving.passport.title: Write your new address in your passport
task.moving.passport.detail: Cross out the old address on page {page} and write the new one above it, without correction fluid. Moving doesn’t make your passport invalid.
task.moving.ircc.title: Update your address with IRCC
task.moving.ircc.detail: If IRCC can’t reach you, documents could be delayed or lost, and your application could be refused or considered abandoned.
task.moving.province.title: Update your health card and driver’s licence
task.moving.province.detail: These come from your province or territory, so contact them to change your address.
task.moving.others.title: Update other federal services you use
task.moving.others.detail: Veterans benefits, firearms licences, NEXUS, boat licences and more each need their own update.
task.moving.expenses.title: Claim your moving expenses
task.moving.expenses.detail: You may be able to deduct them if your new home is at least {km} km closer to your new work or school.
task.moving.sin.title: Your SIN record
task.moving.sin.detail: No update needed for a new address, unless you’re waiting for a SIN confirmation letter by mail.
task.baby.register.title: Register your baby’s birth
task.baby.register.detail: Parents must register the birth with their province or territory. Some provinces offer a newborn registration service that also applies for child benefits and a SIN at the same time.
task.baby.ccb.title: Apply for the Canada child benefit
task.baby.ccb.detail: A tax-free monthly payment for children under 18. Apply as soon as your baby is born. Through birth registration, you don’t need to send proof of birth.
task.baby.sin.title: Get your baby’s SIN
task.baby.sin.detail: In a province, request it when you register the birth. In a territory, apply directly with Service Canada.
task.baby.ei.title: Apply for EI maternity and parental benefits
task.baby.ei.detail: Apply as soon as you stop working: after {weeks} weeks, you may lose benefits. Parental benefits are standard (up to {stdShared} weeks shared between parents, {std} for one parent, up to {stdMax} a week) or extended (up to {extShared} weeks shared, {ext} for one parent, up to {extMax} a week).
task.baby.ei.note: In Quebec, apply to the Quebec Parental Insurance Plan instead.
task.baby.qpip.title: Apply to the Quebec Parental Insurance Plan
task.baby.qpip.detail: In Quebec, maternity, paternity and parental benefits come from the province, not Employment Insurance.
task.baby.health.title: Get your baby’s health card
task.baby.health.detail: Health cards come from your province or territory.
task.baby.passport.title: Apply for a child passport
task.baby.passport.detail: It’s valid for up to {years} years and can’t be renewed, so you apply again when it expires.
task.baby.resp.title: Open an RESP to get education grants
task.baby.resp.detail: When you open a Registered Education Savings Plan, ask your financial institution to apply for the Canada Education Savings Grant and the Canada Learning Bond.
task.baby.provincial.title: Provincial and territorial child benefits
task.baby.provincial.detail: No separate application: when you apply for the Canada child benefit, the CRA checks if you qualify for related programs.
task.marriage.marital.title: Tell the CRA your new marital status
task.marriage.marital.detail: It’s due by the end of the month after your status changes. This includes becoming common-law: living together for {months} months, or having a child together.
task.marriage.sin.title: Update your SIN record with your new name
task.marriage.sin.detail: The law requires it when you change your legal name. It’s free, and online takes about {sinDays} business days.
task.marriage.craName.title: Tell the CRA your new name
task.marriage.craName.detail: It can’t be done online. Call {phone} if you’ve never changed one of your names before, or if you’re going back to a birth name the CRA has on file. Otherwise, or to change both your first and last names, send proof by mail or fax.
task.marriage.passport.title: Get a passport in your new name
task.marriage.passport.detail: You can’t renew with a different name, so apply for a new adult passport.
task.marriage.elections.title: Update your voter registration
task.marriage.elections.detail: Update your name, and your address if you’re moving in together.
task.marriage.recalc.title: Your benefit and credit payments
task.marriage.recalc.detail: Once the CRA has your new status, it recalculates payments like the Canada child benefit, starting the month after your status changed.
task.job-loss.apply.title: Apply for Employment Insurance
task.job-loss.apply.detail: Apply online now, even without your record of employment. You can send documents after you apply.
task.job-loss.estimate.title: Estimate your EI benefits
task.job-loss.estimate.detail: The EI Benefits Estimator shows which benefit may fit you, a possible weekly amount and how many weeks.
task.job-loss.msca.title: Follow your claim in My Service Canada Account
task.job-loss.msca.detail: Check your claim status and messages, and see your records of employment.
task.job-loss.report.title: Complete your EI reports every 2 weeks
task.job-loss.report.detail: Report any work, earnings and your availability to keep getting benefits.
task.job-loss.jobbank.title: Search for work on Job Bank
task.job-loss.jobbank.detail: Free job search, alerts and tools from the Government of Canada.
task.job-loss.finder.title: Check for other help
task.job-loss.finder.detail: The Benefits Finder asks a few questions and lists federal programs that could help you.
task.job-loss.roe.title: Your record of employment
task.job-loss.roe.detail: Your employer submits it, not you. Don’t wait for it before you apply.
task.retiring.estimate.title: Estimate your retirement income
task.retiring.estimate.detail: The Canadian Retirement Income Calculator helps you plan with your public pensions and savings.
task.retiring.when.title: Choose when to start your CPP
task.retiring.when.detail: Any time from age {min} to {max}. Each month before {std65} lowers payments by {early}%; each month after raises them by {late}%.
task.retiring.msca.title: Sign up for My Service Canada Account
task.retiring.msca.detail: You’ll use it to apply for CPP and to manage Old Age Security online.
task.retiring.cpp.title: Apply for your CPP retirement pension
task.retiring.cpp.detail: It doesn’t start on its own. You can apply up to {applyMonths} months before your chosen start date.
task.retiring.oas.title: Watch for your Old Age Security letter
task.retiring.oas.detail: Most people are enrolled automatically and get a letter around their 64th birthday. No letter a month later? Contact Service Canada.
task.retiring.gis.title: Check the Guaranteed Income Supplement
task.retiring.gis.detail: A monthly tax-free payment for people 65 or older with a low income. In most cases, you’re enrolled automatically.
task.retiring.rrsp.title: Decide what happens to your RRSP
task.retiring.rrsp.detail: By the end of the year you turn {age}, choose an option such as a RRIF or an annuity. Your RRSP issuer can explain yours.
task.retiring.scams.title: Protect yourself from scams
task.retiring.scams.detail: Learn how to spot and report scams, and keep your personal information safe.
task.death.cra.title: Tell the CRA the date of death
task.death.cra.detail: Call {phone} and choose any option, or mail Form RC4111. Do it as soon as you can, even if they didn’t get benefits.
task.death.cppOas.title: Cancel their CPP and Old Age Security
task.death.cppOas.detail: Call {cppPhone}. Benefits are paid for the month of death; any payment after that must be repaid.
task.death.deathBenefit.title: Apply for the CPP death benefit
task.death.deathBenefit.detail: The executor should apply within {days} days. It’s a one-time payment of {basic} if they paid into the CPP long enough. Another {topUp} is added only if they never received a CPP or QPP pension or disability benefit and left no spouse or partner who qualifies for a survivor’s pension.
task.death.passport.title: Return their passport
task.death.passport.detail: Mail it to Passport Program, Gatineau QC K1A 0G3, with a copy of the death certificate and a note saying whether to destroy it or send it back.
task.death.survivor.title: Apply for CPP survivor benefits
task.death.survivor.detail: A spouse or common-law partner may get a monthly survivor’s pension. Dependent children may get benefits until 18, or until 25 if they’re in school full-time or part-time.
task.death.allowance.title: Check the Allowance for the Survivor
task.death.allowance.detail: A monthly tax-free payment for a surviving spouse or partner aged {allowMin} to {allowMax} with a low income.
task.death.sin.title: Report the death to the SIN program
task.death.sin.detail: Send proof of death by mail or bring it to a Service Canada Centre. In a province, vital statistics does this for you.
task.death.sin.detailAuto: When a death happens in a province, vital statistics tells the SIN program for you.
task.death.finalReturn.title: File their final tax return
task.death.finalReturn.detail: For a death from January to October, it’s due April 30 of the next year. For November or December, it’s due 6 months after the date of death. If they or their spouse or partner ran a business, it’s June 15 (or 6 months after, if that’s later), but any balance owing is still due on the regular date. A due date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.
task.death.represent.title: Act for them with the CRA the right way
task.death.represent.detail: Don’t sign in to their CRA account. The legal representative, usually the executor, notifies the CRA and gets access to their tax records.
task.death.benefits.title: Most CRA benefit payments
task.death.benefits.detail: Reporting the date of death to the CRA generally takes care of them. Return any payment that still arrives in their name.

count.done.final-return: Done: the final return is filed
